COMMON JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed these two claim petitions U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3696/2022 and death of one Smt.L.Ramakka W/o L.Venkataswami, in M.V.C.
No.3697/2022, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02 . Since these two cases are arising out of one and same accident and cause of action are the same and the respondents are the same and to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and to avoid outcome of conflicting Judgments, these two cases are clubbed together.
M.V.C.No.3697/2022 clubbed with original M.V.C.No.3696/2022 and common evidence came to be recorded in the said cases.
These two cases are proceeded for disposal by way of common Judgment.

03 . The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
 That on 18.02.2022 the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3696/2022 was riding a TVS Super XL Moped bearing No.KA-01-HZ-0622 along with his wife i.e., L.Ramakka in M.V.C.No.3697/2022 as pillion  (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3696/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3697/2022 Venkateswami .L vs Pavan Kumar Dubisetty on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45522397/
2 rider, were going towards their Village Nagireddipalli from Keeluholali Village on the correct side of the road,
on the way at about 11.10 a.m, when they reached near Devarayasamudra Gate, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, the petitioner stopped his said moped to enter into Bengaluru - Mulabagal NH-75 Road, after assuring no vehicles were near to him, he was slowly,
cautiously entering into said Highway.

At that time one Mahindra XUV500 Car bearing No.KA-03-ND-5743 came from Bengaluru side, driven by its driver, at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, the driver of the said Car lost control over his vehicle and went to its wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the said moped.
Due to impact, both were fell down and sustained grievous injuries and said L.Ramakka succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3696/2022 was taken to Government hospital, Mulabagal and after first aid he was shifted to R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar and after several examinations injuries were found and was treated conservatively as an inpatient by applying above knee slab to right lower limb and discharged on 21.02.2022.

He was admitted at Sree Ramadevi Multi Super  (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3696/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3697/2022 Speciality hospital, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, on 22.02.2022 and has undergone surgery for right tibia and he was treated as an inpatient and discharged on 02.03.2022.

On the next day i.e., on 03.03.2022 he was again admitted to the above said hospital for the second time, due to severe pain at fracture site and undergone surgery for right clavicle and treated as an inpatient and discharged on 09.03.2022.

Thereafter,
till today he is under treatment as an outpatient and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment,
medicine, conveyance etc., and further he need about Rs.1,00,000/- towards future treatment and removal of implants.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 65 years and was a Coolie working under different employers and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, till today he is bedridden and lost his earnings and cannot work as earlier due to disability and impediment.
The petitioners in M.V.C.No.3697/2022 have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral, obsequies.

In near future she would have earned more than Rs.40,000/- p.m.
The petitioners were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
After her death, the petitioners do not have any other source of income for their livelihood and are put lot of mental agony and untold misery.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Mahindra Car and in this regard the Mulabagal Rural Police have registered a case against driver of the offending car.

On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections in both the petitions.

The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, income, occupation of deceased and petitioner, manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle, expenses incurred by the petitioners,

the owner of the said vehicle by knowingly entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having the valid and effective driving licence and hence, there is breach of violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner.
The accident in question was not occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle.

11. Issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.3697/2022:-
Petitioner No.1 in M.V.C.No.3697/2022 filed affidavit stated that, he is the husband and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.

To prove the said facts, he has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of deceased and other petitioners and Ration card as per Ex.P.15 to 19 which shows that the petitioners are the father and major son and married daughter of the deceased.
There is no elicited in the cross-examination regarding dependency of the petitioners with the deceased.

As per the recent Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court even the major sons and married daughters are entitled to claim  (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3696/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3697/2022 compensation for the death of their parents on all Venkateswami .L vs Pavan Kumar Dubisetty on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45522397/

12. Issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.3696/2022 and Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.3697/2022:-
The petitioner as well as petitioner No.1 in both cases got himself examined as PW.1 and he has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and he has reiterated the petitions averments therein.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, he and deceased sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and L.Ramakka died on the spot.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Mulbagal Rural Police against driver of the offending Car.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car, the accident took place and petitioner and deceased sustained injuries.

Ex.P.4 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident and both vehicles got damaged.

Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner in M.V.C.No.3696/2022 sustained 1) Lacerated wound of 5 x 3 cm right leg distal 3 rd region exposing soft tissue,
2) 1 x 1 cm lacerated wound present over right leg with no acute bleed, 3) Laceration of 3 x 2 cm over left temporal region and 4) Laceration of 4 x 1 cm over palmar aspect of right hand

sentences.text: To disprove the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.2 did not lead any evidence.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the petitioner and deceased sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, these Issues are answered in the affirmative.
Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.3696/2022:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 65 years and was a Coolie working under different employers and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.,.
Due to accidental injuries, till today he is bedridden and lost his earnings and cannot work as earlier due to disability and impediment.
14 . It is the duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.16 Aadhaar card.

Even though the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1956 and the alleged accident was Venkateswami .L vs Pavan Kumar Dubisetty on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45522397/

Therefore, considering the  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3696/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3697/2022 said document, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 66 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 66 and above is '5'.

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2022 to be taken as Rs.15,500/-
p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,500/- and it is multiplied by 12.
 16.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained a) Open type IIIB comminuted displaced fracture both bones right leg at middle 3rd and lower 3rd junction and b) Closed undisplaced right clavicle fracture at middle 3rd session and he assessed  (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3696/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3697/2022 total disability of both right sided upper and lower limbs at 58% and that of the whole body at 29% and he has produced OPD card with examination report and X-ray as per Ex.P.22 and 23.
In his cross-examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally.
Age of the petitioner is 65 years.
It is partly admits that the person is 65 years restriction movements are common.
Both bones are surgery.
There is no implants and fractures are united and denied to the suggestion that 58% of disability is higher side and he has assessed 1/3rd.
There is no necessity of future surgery.

However, considering the evidence of PW.3, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 1/3rd i.e., 19%. Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 5 x 19%/100 = Rs.1,76,700/-.
 17.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has Venkateswami .L vs Pavan Kumar Dubisetty on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45522397/

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount  (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3696/2022  c/w M.V.C.No.3697/2022 towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.
18. Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and as per X-ray and on account of accidental injuries,
petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to fractures suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.
19. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,500/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 17 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least three months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.46,500/- (Rs.15,500 x 3) under this head.
Medical expenses:- The petitioner has produced entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for Rs.39,185/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.39,185/- under this head.

21. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,

24. Issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.3697/2022:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased L.Ramakka,
who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 55 years and was a Coolie working under different employers and she was also a homemaker and was earning about Rs.25,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral, obsequies.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the major children of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.
